---
title: "Resume a scan"
description: "Let customers continue capture after refreshing the page or returning later."
---

Save the scan ID on your customer’s application record. Once `state.resumable` is true, Bouncr has accepted the first capture and can restore that progress.

## Save progress

In your `onState` handler, persist the ID when the scan becomes resumable. For a single flow in one browser tab, session storage is enough:

```javascript
if (state.resumable && state.scanId) {
  sessionStorage.setItem('bouncrScanId', state.scanId);
}
```

Use a key associated with the application/customer if your product can have several concurrent flows. Clear it on sign-out and after the flow finishes.

## Continue capture

Create a new SDK instance when the customer returns, then pass the saved ID:

```javascript
const scanId = sessionStorage.getItem('bouncrScanId');
capture.start(scanId ?? undefined);
```

Your authorization endpoint checks the customer’s access and returns fresh initialization data for the existing scan. The [backend example](/external/backend) recovers the scan from the signed-in session.

The SDK restores the accepted images and requests the remaining side. If capture is already complete, it proceeds to processing status. A refresh before the first accepted capture requires the customer to capture again.

## Handle another active window

When another window or device takes over the scan, the previous instance enters `Phase.SUPERSEDED`. Show a message directing the customer to continue in the other window. Offer a deliberate **Continue here** action if your product allows switching back.

## Finish the flow

Clear the saved reference once your application has handled completion:

```javascript
onComplete(scanId) {
  sessionStorage.removeItem('bouncrScanId');
  window.location.assign('/onboarding/review');
}
```

Keep the scan ID on your backend record so you can [retrieve its result](/external/results) later.
